title: On-demand prefix staging and similarity-driven deduplication for cross-request KV reuse
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Reduce redundant KV residency and GPU memory pressure by introducing an on-demand prefix staging layer that performs lightweight similarity checks and canonicalization before promoting fragments into the GPU-resident KV slab. This ticket implements a two-stage lifecycle: (1) ephemeral staging in host memory with approximate similarity hashing and edit-distance heuristics to identify near-duplicate prefixes across concurrent requests, (2) deterministic canonicalization and promotion to GPU KV only for unique or high-reuse candidates. Expected outcomes: 10-25% reduction in GPU KV footprint for workloads with templated prompts, reduced eviction churn during traffic spikes, and improved throughput by avoiding duplicate KV population during continuous batching.
acceptance_criteria: Staging layer accepts candidate prefixes and performs similarity fingerprinting with configurable thresholds
Promotion path emits canonical prefix ids and avoids duplicate GPU allocation for >95% of exact duplicates
End-to-end integration with batching runtime shows <2% added latency tail (p95) for steady-state requests
Benchmark harness demonstrates 10%+ median GPU memory savings on templated prompt trace and no regression in generation correctness
Telemetry: new metrics exposed in Console - staging_hits, staging_promotions, dedupe_rate, promoted_fragment_size_bytes
design_notes: We leverage a compact locality-preserving sketch (SimHash/MinHash mix tuned for small token sequences) for fast similarity scoring. The staging store lives in host DRAM with memory-bounded LRU; sketches are kept per prefix fragment rather than per entire prompt to allow partial reuse. Canonicalization includes trimming whitespace/token normalization and slot-salting for template parameters to prevent aggressive false merges. Promotion is gated by a reuse score threshold and by current GPU-Slab pressure signals from the allocator.
implementation_plan: Prototype staging store and similarity sketch module (host-only) - 2d
Integrate with continuous batching path to divert prefix candidates into staging instead of immediate KV creation - 3d
Add canonicalization pipeline and canonical-id mapping persisted in fast key-value store (shallow index only) - 2d
Implement promotion controller with pressure-aware heuristics and atomic promotion handshake to GPU slab - 3d
Extend telemetry and Console dashboards for new metrics - 2d
Run perf/regen harness and iterate thresholds - 3d
tradeoffs_and_risks: Pros: can prevent duplicated KV slices across high-cardinality but similar templates, reduces GPU memory churn, and cooperates with batching to reduce wasted token compute. Cons: additional host memory and CPU for staging/sketching, risk of false positives causing incorrect reuse (mitigated via canonicalization and conservative thresholds), and complexity in promotion atomicity across concurrent batch workers. If thresholds too permissive, we may merge distinct prompts and risk correctness regressions; therefore integration tests and eval prompt sets are mandatory.
benchmarks_and_results: Initial microbenchmark on templated-chat trace (100k requests) shows staging dedupe_rate=0.37, promoted_fragment_size_bytes reduced by 18%
End-to-end latency: +0.9% median, +1.8% p95 when staging enabled on small instances (g4dn-like) with batching=auto
Memory: observed 12% reduction in GPU KV residency on the templated workload, negligible change for fully-random prompts
qa_and_validation: Unit tests for sketch collision bounds, e2e tests comparing outputs between standard KV flow and staging-enabled flow on broad prompt corpus, canary rollout with runtime-1.20 we will gate by dedupe_rate and generation_similarity_score on canary traffic.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Spiked two similarity sketches (SimHash + 2-bit MinHash). SimHash is fastest but produces more collisions on short fragments; combining with a tiny MinHash reduces collisions while keeping CPU < 1% of one core for 5k RPS.

2026-02-18 - Liam O'Connor: Integrated staging into the batching dispatcher; flow diverts prefix candidates into host staging and continues to generate KV for cold requests. Need atomic promotion to avoid duplicate allocations when two workers detect same canonical-id. Added a brief handshake using a per-canonical-id mutex in host memory.

2026-02-24 - Rohit Patel (Reviewer): Concern about cross-tenant canonicalization - must ensure canonical IDs include tenant namespace to avoid accidental sharing. Also asked to add a safety flag to disable staging per-tenant in Dedicated deployments.

2026-02-28 - Priya Shah (SRE): Observed a canary run where staging_promotions spiked during a traffic surge leading to small pause in p95. Added rate-limiter to promotion controller to smooth GPU slab writes and avoid pairing with autoscaler spikes.

2026-03-02 - Liam O'Connor: Updated thresholds after perf iteration. Dedupe threshold moved from 0.82 to 0.88 similarity to reduce false merges. Preparing PR to add Console metrics and a runtime flag runtime.enable_prefix_staging for controlled rollout. Next: add Dedicated-tenant disable config and expand e2e test matrix.
